note: The rubric is the hypothesis; the operator is the data. Entries are append-only. A rubric version with mean |error| > 10 vs the operator is inadmissible at the ship gate (lib/quality-bar.mjs rubricNeedsRevision).

entries.notes: Self-scored by the maker; defect-absence rubric; still-based. Triggered the v2 rebuild + design loop.

entries.artifact: authored hook scene, design-loop cycle 4 (drain frame)
entries.notes: Blind judge, shuffled frames, exemplar anchors by DESCRIPTION only (reference pack empty). Leniency bias: no dimension scored below 6; world-coherence scored 8 from a single frame it cannot assess. Error shrank +39 to +23 across revisions — still inadmissible. Triggered v2.1: comparative judging against REAL reference frames required; unanchored absolute scores inadmissible.

entries.artifact: authored hook scene, design-loop cycle 4 (same frames as prior entry)
entries.notes: First comparative judgment: c4 frames on screen WITH vox-ok + harris-hawaii reference frames (assets/reference-pack), stillJudgeable dims only (ideation 4, composition 5, type 5, finish 4). Error inside ±10 for the first time and HARSH rather than lenient — the safe direction. NOT a blind pair: the judge knew the operator's 53 when scoring, so this validates the protocol's direction, not its calibration. v2.1 stays provisional until a blind pair (next artifact scored by operator before the judge) lands inside ±10.

entries.artifact: authored hook scene, design-loop cycle 7 (slam + drain frames)
entries.notes: Semi-blind pair: the judge's 65 was visible in the report, and the operator scored 10 below it (weak anchoring). Judge dims: ideation 6.5, composition 6.5, type 7, finish 6. RESIDUAL BIAS NAMED: the same judge was harsh on c4 (operator-anchored) and +10 lenient on its OWN fresh work — maker-as-judge inflation, exactly what design-loop doctrine forbids ('the maker never scores'). Fix: judging moves to a separate context with no loop history (subagent, unlabeled frames). Also recorded: operator REVISED c4 from 53 to 44 after side-by-side viewing ('I actually agree') — agreement with the judge's 44.5, but contaminated as calibration (operator saw the judge's number first), so the c4 entry keeps the original blind 53. v2.1 mean |error| = (8.5+10.4)/2 = 9.45 — admissible by 0.55, not comfortably.

entries.artifact: same c7 frames, re-judged by a SEPARATED judge (fresh context, unlabeled frames, no loop history)
entries.notes: REPLICATION RESULT: the separated judge scored ideation 7 / composition 6 / type 7 / finish 5 = 65.5 — within 0.1 of the maker's 65.4. This WEAKENS the maker-bias hypothesis as the full explanation: the ~+10 residual at this tier is systematic model-judge bias shared across contexts. Also note the spread: judges saw c4→c7 as +21 (44.5→65.5); the operator saw +11 (44→55) — judges over-credit improvement. Two pairs cannot separate offset from gain; next blind pair decides. The separated judge's qualitative read converged with the operator's: 'flawless vector cleanliness is the single loudest tell', 'one centered card floating in inert darkness', fix = composite the actual archival scan (1872 Statutes at Large is public domain — publishable, not research-only).

entries.artifact: authored hook scene, design-loop cycle 8 — the MOTION pass, scored as a 9s CLIP (first clip-class entry)
entries.notes: No judge pair (under v2.2 the judge is a ranker; no clip-judging protocol exists yet, and the maker deliberately did not self-score). Ground truth for the clip class: c7 stills 55 -> c8 clip 61. The motion pass (slam physics, hyphen fragments, pen easing, handheld drift, ink behavior, counter settle) bought +6 operator points. Cycle 9 targets the convergent finding: material truth via the real public-domain 1872 statute scan.

entries.artifact: authored hook scene, cycle 9 — substrate replaced with the REAL 1872 statute page (LoC scan, public domain); judged by a fresh separated judge (unlabeled frames, no loop history)
entries.notes: Judge dims: ideation 8 ('argues with real evidence the way the references do' — first 8 on any dimension), composition 6 (dead vignette hotspot; slip ends mid-air; drip doesn't land on the stat), type 7 (added type well-chosen but off-the-shelf vs art-directed reference lettering), finish 6 (overlays betray digital seams: clean slip edge, uniform drip stroke, airbrushed scrim, heavy corner vignette on an otherwise authentic scan). Ranker trend: c7 65.5 -> c9 70.9. OPERATOR RESULT (clip): 71 — error -0.1, the first essentially-exact pair. Caveats recorded: judge scored STILLS, operator scored the CLIP; the operator additionally flagged PACING ('feels a bit off') which stills structurally cannot exhibit — so the agreement is partly coincidental (stills-craft aligned; clip adds a pacing debit and a substrate credit the judge never saw). v2.2-separated mean |error| = (10.5 + 0.1)/2 = 5.3 — ADMISSIBLE. Operator trajectory across the loop: c4 44 -> c7 55 -> c8 61 -> c9 71. Pacing diagnosis vs beat sheet: the ellipse (verdict) precedes the slam (evidence) at 0.6s vs 1.9s, and the final ~5s is a flat counter tail. Cycle 10 = re-choreography (discovery -> evidence -> judgment -> consequence) + material integration + ink wicks along the line and drips INTO the counter.

entries.artifact: authored hook scene, cycle 10 (final budgeted) — re-choreography + material pass; judged by a fresh separated judge on post-fix clip-extracted stills
entries.notes: Judge dims: ideation 7 (evidence-argument real but 'staged on a single document scan' — thinner than multi-material references), composition 6 (the stat sits on a 'formless dark smudge' colliding with page text), type 7 (only original type is a UI-ish sans label vs bespoke genre lockups), finish 6 (torn edges too subtle — read razor-straight; scrim reads airbrushed). RANKER READING: c10 stills at/below c9 stills (66.4 vs 70.9; note inter-judge variance — c9's judge gave the same substrate ideation 8, c10's gave 7), while ALL of c10's intended changes are MOTION (story order, wick, drip-to-counter) which stills cannot exhibit. OPERATOR RESULT (clip): 74 — error -7.6, inside the gate, harsh side. THE RANKER INVERTED (judge c10<c9, operator 74>71) on a motion-dominated cycle: stills-only ranking is unreliable when the cycle's changes are temporal — clip-class judging protocol needed. OPERATOR CRITIQUE (new dimension exposed): 'hard to read, not easy to digest, not clear enough visually what it means' — COMPREHENSION. Judges scored ideation as craft-of-evidence; the operator scores first-viewing meaning. v2.3 refinement: the judge must state what a MUTED first-time viewer would think the scene means; if it cannot, visual-ideation caps at 5. The scene never shows: what the document is, that Congress meant 'fruit-plants' (seedlings), that the comma made fruit itself duty-free. Cycle 11 (operator-extended budget) = the clarity pass: context beat, intended-vs-printed transformation (hyphen pops out, comma slams in), plain-language meaning line.

entries.artifact: authored hook scene, cycle 11 — the CLARITY pass (context card, mechanism lockup, meaning line, 330f); judged under v2.3 comprehension-first protocol
entries.notes: COMPREHENSION TEST PASSED: asked what a muted first-time viewer would understand, the judge recited the intended story nearly verbatim ('In 1872... a clerk printed the line as fruit, plants — and that single comma made every imported fruit duty-free, at a cost to the Treasury...'). That sentence was exactly what the operator said was missing at c10. Craft dims: ideation 7, composition 6, type 7, finish 5 = 65.5. Stills-blindness recurs: the judge reported the mechanism 'stays verbal' because the hyphen-pop/label-swap is temporal, and read the counter at $0 as 'unfinished' (early-count frame). REAL hits to carry into c12: late frames stack five overlays (declutter — retire the lockup once the meaning line lands); the soft radial scrims are 'airbrushed blobs with no material logic' used three times — replace with one material device (ink-wash/torn-paper); a persistent small 'meant: fruit-plants' ghost would make the contrast survive in stills and help viewers who blink through the pop.

entries.artifact: OPERATOR CRITIQUE-ONLY (no score) on the c11 clip
entries.notes: Operator declined to score; three critiques: (1) 'speed and pacing felt wrong and too fast to digest'; (2) 'the gray shapes looked really bad and made it harder to read' — third independent condemnation of the radial scrims; (3) 'text sizes and orientations still feels not comfortable or interesting' — no type system. Drove cycle 12: 14s pacing with real holds, all radial scrims deleted, one organizing device (editorial voice in a shadowed left column, lighting not shapes), type anchored to a single left margin with deliberate scale hierarchy.

entries.artifact: authored hook scene, cycle 12 — pacing + type system (voice column, 420f/14s); judged under v2.3 comprehension-first
entries.notes: Comprehension PASSED again (verbatim story, including reading the mid-count counter correctly). Dims: ideation 7, composition 5, type 6, finish 6 = 61.8. The composition-5 specifics were real bugs, all fixed in the delivered clip after judging: label drowning in page print (now on a solid accent bar — the references' owned-zone device), no air after the landed comma (words now split apart post-slam), [sic.] fragment colliding with 'duty-free.' (now fades with the ring), inert right half during context (page now ghosts through). Judge's standing directive adopted as the design language going forward: every overlay owns a cleared zone (bars/tabs/masked paper). Ranker caution stands: stills read c12 below c11 while all of c12's changes are pacing/temporal — operator clip verdict decides. OPERATOR RESULT (clip): 82 — error -20.2, the judge's THIRD and largest inversion/miss on a motion-dominated cycle (c10 inverted, c9 lucky-exact, c12 -20.2). DOCTRINE UPDATE: stills-judge scores on temporal cycles are structurally invalid for calibration — recorded as ranker-input only for still-level dims; a clip-class judging protocol (filmstrip minimum) is required before any judge number on a motion cycle enters calibration math. Operator trajectory: 44 -> 55 -> 61 -> 71 -> 74 -> 82. Operator residual at 82: 'still feels hard to digest' — with pacing/type/clarity rebuilt, the remaining digestion load is AUDIO: the clip is silent; the repo's own audio-first doctrine has been inverted in the lab. Cycle 13 = the audio pass (scratch VO, beats re-solved from measured audio, SFX, bed, -14 LUFS).

entries.artifact: authored hook scene, cycle 13 — the AUDIO pass (VO-derived beats, SFX, bed, -14 LUFS master, 34.5s)
entries.notes: OPERATOR: 82, 'no improvement' — delta 0 vs c12. The audio hypothesis is FALSIFIED as scored (audio may still be necessary, but it was not the binding constraint). PLATEAU RULE FIRED (two cycles, delta < epsilon 2): stop patching, re-diagnose at a higher level. Root-cause reread of the four accumulated critiques: every fix so far made TEXT easier to read, but the scene is 100% text-on-text — a full-bleed dense-print page as 34s of wallpaper, typographic overlays on top, and the story's OBJECTS (fruit, money) never once visible. References stage ONE simple subject on a clean field; our eye never rests. Diagnosis: wrong staging + missing concrete imagery. Cycle 14 = re-staging, same VO/timing (controlled experiment): dark stage as home, the page as a PROP that enters when cited and recedes after the slam, and the meaning beat finally SHOWS the meaning — public-domain period fruit illustrations stamped DUTY-FREE feeding the counter. If the score still doesn't move with staging + imagery + audio all in place, the binding constraint is voice performance (the named next build).

entries.artifact: authored hook scene, cycle 14 — re-staging + concrete imagery (page as prop; USDA fruit exhibits stamped duty-free), same VO/timing as c13
entries.notes: REGRESSION: 82 -> 79. Operator critique (fullest yet): (1) 'timing and pacing very wrong and too sluggish' — the c11 'too fast' correction overshot: 0.96x voice + 2.2s gaps + 4.6s tail = sluggish; (2) 'wasn't synced well' — CONFIRMED MECHANICAL DEBT: all word timings are char-weighted ESTIMATES, never measurements; slam/stamps/reveals land on guesses; (3) 'a lot of silence and dead air waiting for the next piece' — beat-island structure with near-silent bed; (4) 'not visually interesting, doesn't keep my eye throughout' — nothing develops during gaps (retention doctrine: something must always be in motion); (5) 'isn't explaining the WHY or the HOW — falling flat even though it's a cool story' — the SCRIPT: never explains hyphen=one-item vs comma=two-items, never shows the refund mechanism (lawyers demanded refunds of paid duties). Cycle 15 = script rewrite (cold-open on the $40M, mechanism beat, lawyers beat, stinger) + EXACT sync by construction (sync-critical words synthesized as separate segments with known start times — no estimates, no ASR dependency) + tightened gaps at 1.0x + continuous-motion rule. The re-staging itself is retained (exhibits/prop staging not named as a problem).

entries.artifact: authored hook scene, cycle 15 — the story pass (why/how script, exact segment sync, 50.5s)
entries.notes: NEW HIGH: 79 -> 83.9, 'you're getting close' — 3.1 from the 87 bar. The script/sync/continuous-motion rebuild moved +4.9. Remaining critique, unusually specific: (1) 'pacing still felt wrong' in places; (2) 'some of it still felt flat and dead, like the fruit plant part' — CONFIRMED against the beat map: the law act's 'congress' segment is 7.7s of slow page-zoom with a static lockup, the longest undeveloped stretch; (3) 'animation and visualization and text presentation still isn't super easy to digest or feel good or fully engaging' — kinetic craft: uniform entrances, no secondary motion (cards don't react to their stamps), no micro-emphasis. Cycle 16 = the dead-middle rebuild (congress split into 3 sync segments; animated list-scan highlight stepping down the page entries as the VO says 'the list of what gets taxed'; TARIFF ACT bar stamp; hyphen pulse on the word 'hyphenated') + kinetic polish pass (snappier springs, scale-in text, stamp reactions on cards, counter crossings pulse). Trajectory: 44 -> 55 -> 61 -> 71 -> 74 -> 82 -> 82 -> 79 -> 83.9.

entries.artifact: authored hook scene, cycle 16 — dead-middle rebuild + kinetic polish (55.3s)
entries.notes: Nominal 85.5 (new high, +1.6). DIRECTION AFFIRMED: 'I like where you're going... bigger text, keeping things centered, visualizations and animations — it just needs to do MORE of it.' Gap named: 'not visually engaging enough, still doesn't feel like a pro YouTube video' — density: pro hooks present a fresh designed visual composition every ~2.5-4s; ours has ~7 setups in 55s with segments riding earlier setups.

OPERATOR RE-ANCHORS THE METER: 'We may need to reorganize the score to move back by 10 points including all of the last ones because we are getting close to the gate and I still think we're far from it.' Adopted: all design-loop clip scores in the recent high cluster shift -10 as working ground truth; the 87 gate is UNCHANGED. Restated working series: c12 82->72, c13 82->72, c14 79->69, c15 83.9->73.9, c16 85.5->75.5 — current position ~11.5 points from the gate, matching the operator's felt distance. ASSUMPTION (documented, correctable): the rescale window covers the c12+ clip series where 'getting close' compression built; earlier scores (c4 44 ... c10 74) and the pre-loop 39 are left nominal pending operator correction. Doctrine note: this is the calibration system working — the meter re-zeroing beats a meter drifting into the gate; all rubric-vs-operator error math for affected pairs must use rescaled values going forward (c9's 70.9-vs-71 pair sits at the boundary; if 71 rescales to 61 the judge error becomes +9.9 — still inside +/-10).
